newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to complete $5.5 bln repayment this month.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to complete $5.5 bln repayment this month.

text.p: Kuwait will finish paying back a $5.5 billion sovereign loan on time in December, the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Tuesday.
"The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) Director General Ali al-Bader said today (Tuesday) the state will repay the last instalment of the state loan during the current month," it said.
"The Kuwaiti economy has recovered and there is no need for such a loan," the agency quoted Bader as saying.
Kuwait's Central Bank has said it will not borrow from foreign markets again.

Kuwait's 1991 jumbo loan arranged by J.P. Morgan and Co follwing Iraq's 1990-91 occupation of the tiny oil-rich state. At that time the loan was the largest ever made by commercial banks to a sovereign state.
The main lending banks were from Japan, France, Germany and the United States and some Arab countries. Some 80 banks took part in the loan used for reconstruction projects.
"The loan repayment was done using state and investment revenue without a need to liquidate assets," said Bader.
KIA, which manages the country's external debt, is in charge of Kuwait's estimated $35 billion foreign investment portfolio.
